record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Universal algorithms for multivariate integration have been constructed for the cube [0,1]^d. Do there exist universal algorithms of the same kind for integration over domains other than [0,1]^d?

evidence.quote: Open Problem: So far only the domain [0,1]d was studied for the construction of universal algorithms. One might speculate that universal algorithms also exist for other domains.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $d\ge 1$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of function classes $F\subset L_1(\Omega,\mu)$, where $(\Omega,\mu)$ is a measure space and each $F$ consists of integrable functions $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. A (deterministic) cubature/algorithm based on $n$ function values is a map
$$Q_n(f)=\phi_n\bigl(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n)\bigr),$$
where $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\Omega$ and $\phi_n:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ (the sample points may be chosen adaptively). The worst-case error of $Q_n$ on a class $F$ is
$$e(Q_n,F)=\sup_{f\in F}\Bigl|\int_\Omega f\,d\mu-Q_n(f)\Bigr|,$$
and the $n$-th minimal error is $e_n(F)=\inf_{Q_n}e(Q_n,F)$. A sequence of algorithms $(Q_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is called \emph{universal} for the family $\mathcal{F}$ if, for every $F\in\mathcal{F}$, one has
$$e(Q_n,F)\;\asymp\;e_n(F)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
i.e.\ $(Q_n)$ achieves the optimal order of convergence on every class $F\in\mathcal{F}$ simultaneously, without knowledge of $F$. (Analogous definitions apply in the randomized setting using expected errors.)

Known case. For $\Omega=[0,1]^d$ with Lebesgue measure, universal algorithms have been constructed for natural scales $\mathcal{F}$ of smoothness classes (e.g.\ weighted Korobov, Sobolev, and Besov classes), simultaneously attaining the optimal order on every class in the family.

Problem. Determine whether universal algorithms exist when the integration domain is not the unit cube. More precisely: exhibit a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ (or more generally a measure space) other than $[0,1]^d$, together with a natural family $\mathcal{F}$ of function classes on $\Omega$ (for instance, smoothness classes on the Euclidean ball, the sphere, the simplex, or an unbounded domain such as $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a Gaussian weight), and a sequence $(Q_n)$ of cubature rules using $n$ function values that is universal for $\mathcal{F}$ in the above sense; or prove that no such universal sequence can exist for the given family.
artifact.status_search_result: A recent (2024–2025) preprint and journal paper "A simple universal algorithm for high-dimensional integration" still treats the cube $[0,1]^d$, and earlier universal-algorithm constructions (Krieg–Novak; Dũng; Ullrich and coauthors) likewise focus on the cube. No construction of an analogous universal algorithm for non-cube domains was located, consistent with the problem being posed as open.

status_evidence.title: A simple universal algorithm for high-dimensional integration
status_evidence.snippet: Universal algorithm with optimal rate on weighted Korobov classes on the cube [0,1]^d.
status_evidence.claim: Recent universal-algorithm constructions remain restricted to the cube domain.

status_evidence.title: A Universal Algorithm for Multivariate Integration
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a universal cubature on [0,1]^d simultaneously optimal on several smoothness scales.
status_evidence.claim: Existing universal algorithms are stated for the unit cube.
